title: Chat and communication
content: Most of Mysterria is people talking to each other. Keep it bearable.

title: Harassment
content: Insulting people, following someone around to pick fights, or joining a pile-on. One heated argument is not harassment. Carrying on after someone has asked you to stop is.

ladder.case: A one-off insult in a bad moment
Going after the same person repeatedly
Organising others to do it with you

title: Swearing
content: Swearing is fine. Sexual talk and relentless filth are not, and neither is a slur with a joke wrapped around it.

title: Spam
content: Repeating yourself, flooding a channel, or playing noise over voice.

title: Private messages
content: Harassment in DMs counts exactly as much as harassment in public. Block the person and open a ticket instead of trading insults.

title: Names, avatars and skins
content: Nothing offensive, extremist or pornographic. Staff will ask you to change it first.

ladder.case: You change it when asked
You refuse to change it
Extremist or pornographic to begin with

title: Building and the world
content: What you build is permanent for everyone else too.

title: Offensive builds
content: Extremist symbols and pornographic structures come down, and whoever placed them answers for it.

ladder.case: A crude joke, removed when asked
Extremist symbols or sexual content

title: Griefing and stealing
content: Breaking what someone else built, or taking what is not yours. Consent changes this entirely: agreed wars and agreed raids are not griefing.

ladder.case: Minor damage, returned or repaired
Destroying or looting someone's build
Wiping a town or emptying its vaults

title: Lag machines
content: Farms and contraptions that hurt server performance, and chunk loaders nobody approved.

ladder.case: Careless build, taken down when asked
Built deliberately to lag the server

title: Cheating
content: Everything here is about taking something the game did not give you.

title: Cheats and hacks
content: X-ray, kill aura, reach, autoclickers, macros, and anything else that plays the game for you.

title: Abusing a bug
content: Find a glitch and report it in the bug forum. Reports are rewarded. Using one instead is the offence, and how far you take it decides what it costs you.

ladder.case: You triggered it once and reported it yourself
You kept using it after you knew
You duped anything of value
You handed out duped items or taught the method

title: Accounts and privacy
content: One person, one account, and nothing about anyone's real life without their say-so.

title: Personal information
content: Do not post someone's real name, address, photographs, workplace or other accounts. Not as a threat, not as a joke, not as proof of anything.

title: Coordinating outside the game
content: Planning raids, trades, wars and town business in Discord is ordinary play and always allowed. Organising a group against one person, or manufacturing evidence to get someone punished, is not.

title: Alt accounts
content: One account each. Alts exist to be caught, so assume they will be.

ladder.case: An alt that gained you nothing
Extra plots, extra event rewards, extra votes
Evading a ban or a mute

title: Pretending to be someone else
content: Copying another player's name and skin to trade on their reputation, or passing yourself off as staff.

ladder.case: A joke that gets cleared up immediately
Impersonating another player
Impersonating staff

title: Community conduct
content: The rules that are not about mechanics at all.

title: Hate speech
content: Slurs, and attacks on race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, gender or sexuality. There is no ironic version of this rule.

title: False reports
content: Reporting something you believe happened is always fine, even if you turn out to be wrong. Inventing it is not.

ladder.case: An honest mistake
A report you knew was false
Faked screenshots or edited logs

title: Arguing with staff
content: Disagreeing with a decision is not an offence, and a ticket will get it read. Abusing the person who made it is the offence.

title: Begging
content: Asking once is asking. Asking eight people in a row for items, ranks or free potions is spam.

title: Real money trading
content: Accounts, items and currency are not for sale for real money. The shop is the only place value enters the server from outside.

title: Channels and promotion
content: Where things go, and what cannot be posted anywhere.

title: Wrong channel
content: Posts in the wrong place get moved. Doing it on purpose and repeatedly is spam.

title: Advertising
content: Other servers, paid services and referral links.

ladder.case: Answering a friend who asked where you play
Posting an advert in chat
Mass DMing members

title: Warnings and bans
content: Every rule above carries a number. This chapter is what those numbers do.

title: How warnings add up
content: Warnings stack. Eight of them bans you permanently from both the Minecraft server and the Discord, and waiting does not reverse that ban. A warning expires six months after it was issued, so what counts is how many you hold now, not how many you have ever been given.

title: What each warning costs
content: One: the warning alone. Two: a 2 hour mute. Three: a 4 hour mute... The next consequent warning doubles the punishment. Eight: permanent ban, on both platforms.

title: Why one rule can cost different amounts
content: Several rules carry a range, because the same rule has to cover a careless mistake and a deliberate campaign. Where a rule shows a range, the marker beside it lists what each amount is for.

title: Appeals
content: Open a ticket in Discord. An admin who was not involved reviews it, and warnings can be reduced or lifted. Reductions and unbans are posted publicly beside the original punishment. Once an appeal has been decided, that decision stands.

title: Affiliated servers
content: Towns and communities we link to are still full of our players.

title: Staff presence
content: Any server or community promoted inside Mysterria must carry a Mysterria staff member with audit log access. That is the price of being promoted here.

title: Conduct elsewhere
content: Slurs, hate speech and doxxing on an affiliated server are punished here exactly as if they had happened here.

title: Losing affiliate status
content: A community that will not moderate itself, or refuses staff oversight, loses its approved status and its links come down.

title: PvP and incursions
content: PvP exists in announced zones, Cosmos Incursions, and town claims where the owner has switched it on. Everywhere else it is off. Entering a zone is consent to fight, and nothing else is.

title: Consent is the zone
content: Inside a PvP zone anyone may attack you, and that is what the zone is for. Outside one, any ability that damages, drains or debuffs another player is an attack, whatever the ability is called.

title: Dragging people into a fight
content: Teleporting, pulling or pushing someone into a PvP zone, or into a fight they are not part of, without their agreement.

title: Spectators and the dead
content: If you are dead, spectating or otherwise out of the fight and can't be harmed, you are out of it. Draining, cursing, buffing or scouting from that state is not allowed.

title: Effects that follow you out
content: An effect that landed on you inside a zone stays on you when you leave, and that is fair - you were in the zone when it was applied. What it does not buy is control of that player once they are outside. Steering someone with it, above all into a zone where dying costs them more than where they started, is the offence.

title: Locking others out of event mechanics
content: Holding a beacon, capture point or objective so that no other player can reach it and no other player can stop you. The test is whether any counter exists at all, not whether it is hard.

ladder.case: A strong position others can still break
No counterplay left for anyone
Doing it from a state where you cannot be harmed

title: Abilities known to be broken
content: Once an ability is publicly known to be bugged, using it in PvP is bug abuse under 3.2 rather than clever play. Reporting it is worth more than the fight is.
